question: What level of army is needed to take down a Balrog?
notes: Balrog: combat skill 6, resistance 6 to melee/energy/spirit/weather, 5 to riding, 0 to ranged; 200 melee attacks/round, 280 hits, tactics 5; casts hellfire at level 4 (2-200 energy attacks). Hit odds: equal skill 1:1, each level of difference doubles (rules § Combat > The Battle). Sources: gamedata.cpp MonDefs Balrog entry, engine ItemDescription(BALR).

question: If I want to kill a monster and loot its lair, is it enough to just issue the order ATTACK <unitnum>?
notes: ATTACK only reaches units in the same region, so move there first. A monster inside a lair (any object except O_DUMMY) is always visible and always catchable: faction.cpp CanSee sets retval 1 for units in non-dummy objects, and CanCatch returns 1 for them, so stealth/observation and riding don't matter. Lairs cannot be entered and give no protection (ObjectDefs Lair/Cave protect 0). There is no separate lair loot: treasure comes as battle spoils, i.e. random silver up to the monster's silver value plus possibly a random item of its spoil type (army.cpp GetMonSpoils), plus about half of the items the dead carried (battle.cpp GetSpoils). Winners only pick up spoils they can carry, per the SPOILS order (unit.cpp CanGetSpoil). Earlier notes wrongly said see/catch checks could fail; the baseline answer was right. A 'needs riding' forbidden pattern was dropped: it flagged two correct statements about wandering monsters and caught nothing wrong.

question: What should I consider when defending against an army with SSTO?
notes: SSTO = summon storm (Weather Lore spell). Engine description: between 2 and 100 times the mage's skill level weather attacks; each hit gives the target storm (-2 attack, -2 versus melee) for the rest of the battle; it doesn't target units already affected. Defense: resistance/shields against weather attacks, armor saves vs weather, the attacker's mage count and level. Baseline (local Qwen, before compendium) wrongly claimed 'no direct damage' and 'ranged troops are unaffected'.

question: How many months does it take a 10-man unit to reach COMB 3 from scratch without a teacher, and how much silver does the studying cost?
notes: Level 1 needs 1 month, level 2 two more, level 3 three more: 6 months. Combat costs $10 per man per month: 10 x 10 x 6 = $600, plus maintenance (rules § Skills > Studying).

question: How many mages can a faction have if it puts 3 points into magic?
notes: New Origins faction points: Magic 3 = 4 mages / 7 apprentices (neworigins/rules.cpp am[] and aa[], rules § Playing Atlantis > Factions).

question: What does it cost to study TACTICS, and what does the skill do in battle?
notes: $200 per man per month (rules § Skills > Studying). The better tactician's side gets a free round of attacks (rules § Combat > The Battle; battle.cpp FreeRound).

question: Which items does the standard game enable that are not available by default?
notes: standard/extra.cpp EnableItem calls. The spear is enabled by default already. Mushroom, healing potion, rough gem and gems are only enabled with underworld/underdeep levels, which standard sets to 0 (standard/rules.cpp).

question: A balrog is wandering in the region where my units are. How likely is it to attack us this month, and what decides which unit it goes for?
notes: runorders.cpp Game::CheckWMonAttack: each month a wandering monster that can attack counts the men it can see AND catch (CountWMonTars: only normal, mage and apprentice units; Unit::CanSee/CanCatch in faction.cpp, so stealth above the monster's observation or out-riding it keeps a unit safe). It attacks if getrandom(max(100, 300 - men)) < its hostile value, so the chance is hostile/(300 - men), capped at hostile/100; with 200 or more visible men a hostile-100 monster attacks for certain. The victim is picked by a random man among the targets (GetWMonTar), so bigger units are more likely to be attacked. Unit::Hostile (unit.cpp) returns the MonDefs hostile percent: the Balrog entry in gamedata.cpp MonDefs is {6,{6,6,6,6,5,0}, 200,280,0, 5,1,2, "hellfire",4, 25000,IT_MAGIC,100,1,"Balrog","BALR"...}: silver 25000, hostile 100, number 1. Trap: the Compendium text ('the player must be pretty unlucky to be attacked') comes from MonType::getAggression in items.cpp, which multiplies hostile by MONSTER_ADVANCE_HOSTILE_PERCENT (0 in standard/rules.cpp) and floors at MONSTER_ADVANCE_MIN_PERCENT (15); that number governs advancing into regions, not the attack roll. A mustNotMention on 'rarely attack' was dropped: a correct answer may quote the Compendium wording before correcting it.

question: After my army wins a battle, exactly how much of the enemy's stuff do we get and how is it split between my units?
notes: battle.cpp Battle::GetSpoils: for every unit on the losing side, percent = dead/(alive+dead) of each item stack is removed from the unit (soldiers and incomplete ships excluded), and of that about half, (num + getrandom(2))/2, goes into the spoils pile; IT_ALWAYS_SPOIL items give the whole share, IT_NEVER_SPOIL items nothing. Silver has no special treatment (ItemDefs silver is IT_NORMAL|IT_MONEY, weight 0), so winners get roughly half the losers' silver times the losers' casualty fraction. Distribution in army.cpp Army::Lose/Win -> the spoils loop after DoHeal: for each item type a list of eligible units is built with one entry per surviving soldier (so shares are proportional to surviving men), filtered by Unit::CanGetSpoil (unit.cpp: weight-0 items always; FLAG_NOSPOILS takes nothing with weight; WALK/RIDE/FLY/SWIM/SAIL flags compare current load + item weight against the matching capacity, counting the capacity the item itself provides). Weightless items are handed out in equal chunks (num/ns), items with weight one at a time round-robin, and the remainder at random. Rules § Combat says 50% of the dead's items picked up at random in proportion to surviving men; the code detail is the casualty fraction applied to the whole losing unit's inventory and the per-soldier eligibility list.

question: If my unit and another faction's unit both TAX the same region in the same month, how is the money divided, and what caps how much each of us gets?
notes: unit.cpp Unit::Taxers: men count as taxers under WHO_CAN_TAX = TAX_NORMAL (TAX_COMBAT_SKILL | TAX_USABLE_WEAPON, standard/rules.cpp): any Combat skill, or a weapon they have the skill to use; each taxer is worth TAX_BASE_INCOME = 50 (TAX_BONUS_WEAPON/ARMOR/FORT are 0 in standard). runorders.cpp Game::CountTaxes rejects taxing when there is no population, a non-friendly unit is on guard (ARegion::CanTax, aregion.cpp: any guard with attitude <= neutral to you blocks), the faction is over its tax-region limit (ActivityCheck), or the unit has no taxers. Game::RunTaxRegion: desired = max(sum of all taxers' income, region wealth); each unit gets taxers * wealth / desired, i.e. the region's taxable wealth is shared in proportion to each unit's taxing men, no matter which faction or in which order; nobody gets more than 50 per taxing man. Region wealth (economy.cpp ARegion::SetupEconomy/UpdateEconomy) = Population * (Wages - 10*MAINTENANCE_COST) / 50, MAINTENANCE_COST = 10. PILLAGE runs before TAX and sets wealth to 0 (RunPillageRegion, ARegion::Pillage). Rules § Economy > Taxing/Pillaging say 'split evenly among all taxers', which matches the per-man proportional split.

question: My one-man assassin has Stealth 3 and a ring of invisibility. Who can stop the assassination, and what happens when it goes through?
notes: gamedata.cpp AttribDefs: ring of invisibility (RING) adds a constant 3 to stealth (one per man; USE_WORST), amulet of true seeing (AMTS) adds 2 to observation, so the assassin's effective stealth is 6. runorders.cpp Game::Do1Assassinate: the assassin must see the target (CanSee), the target must be a player unit (not city guards or monsters), the assassin must be a 1-man unit. Game::CanSeeSteal collects every faction present whose Faction::CanSee(assassin) is non-zero; CanSee (faction.cpp) returns 2 when a unit's observation is greater than the stealth and 1 when it is equal, so an observer with observation equal to the assassin's stealth already catches him. The attempt fails if the target's faction, a faction allied to the target, or the city guard faction (guardfaction) can see him; the seers are told who tried. HARDER_ASSASSINATION is 0 in standard/rules.cpp, so there is no stealth penalty for assassinating. With a ring, Unit::AmtsPreventCrime (unit.cpp) blocks the attempt if the target has at least one amulet per man (PROPORTIONAL_AMTS_USAGE is 0, so partial coverage never helps). On success Game::RunBattle(..., ass): battle.cpp Battle::FreeRound gives the assassin a free round, armies are built with the assassination flag so only armor usable in assassinations (leather and cloth) counts, spoils via GetSpoils with ass (a ring-bearing assassin cannot loot amulets). Rules § Stealth and Observation > Assassination cover the flow; the code adds the exact ring (+3), amulet (+2), equal-observation and amulet-per-man rules.
